messages:
incident-bot: PAGE FIRED: release-edge rollout - elevated 5xx rate in eu-west-1 canary group :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-48291 triggered (severity: P1) — auto-page to @maya_wong and @devon_choi
maya_wong: acked — I'm on it, joining bridge.  Investigating canary logs and proxy traces.
devon_choi: ack — pulling recent deploy diff, suspect networking change to edge-proxy v2.14.1 that landed in canary.
samir_lee: @maya_wong @devon_choi any customer  impact yet? metrics show ~3% of requests returning 502 across canary hosts.
maya_wong: Customer-facing error rate looks small but spiky. Rolling 5xx p99 increased, latency up ~200ms for affected subset. Putting note in support: "minor but visible".
kena_hart: from logs: backend upstream conn failures, TLS handshake errors intermittently. snippet:
```
2026-03-14T02:10:15Z edge-proxy[pid=2234]: upstream_connect_error: handshake failed: unexpected EOF
2026-03-14T02:10:21Z edge-proxy[pid=2235]: 502 Bad Gateway - upstream read timeout
```
maya_wong: running quick canary isolation: marking one canary shard out of LB for deeper debug.
devon_choi: i repro locally with proxy v2.14.1 when backend cert rotation happens.  Reverted to v2.14.0 locally and it stops.
ops_shift_lead: we should consider rollback of the canary to v2.14.0 if impact continues. who's on rollback?
samir_lee: +1 rollback if spike persists. Do we have automated rollback playbook?
maya_wong: yes — manual rollback command below (will execute after we confirm):
```
# rollback canary instances to previous AMI/image
redwoodctl rollout cancel --release release-edge --target canary-group-eu-west-1
redwoodctl deploy --image edge-proxy:v2.14.0 --group canary-group-eu-west-1
```
pagerduty-bot: INC-48291 escalated to team (2nd page) — no ack from primary in 3 minutes (auto-escalation).
kena_hart: @ops_shift_lead i'll prep rollback bundle and healthcheck override. want to hold 2 more minutes to try an nginx-level workaround (increase upstream timeout) or go straight rollback?
devon_choi: if TLS handshake is root cause, timeout won't fix. i'd rather rollback canary now to stop bleed, then re-run tests in staging for the TLS fix.
maya_wong: agreed. executing rollback in 30s. will update when done.
maya_wong: RUN: redwoodctl deploy --image edge-proxy:v2.14.0 --group canary-group-eu-west-1  (started)
incident-bot: action recorded: deployment rollback initiated by maya_wong (run id: 8f3a2c)
maya_wong: rollback completed — monitoring. canary 5xx dropped back to baseline within 90s. p50/p95 latency normalized.
samir_lee: confirmed — error rate back to 0.2% after rollback. good catch.
ops_shift_lead: good. marking incident as mitigated. opening incident bridge for 30min postmortem and follow-ups.
kena_hart: filing an RFC to add a pre-rollout TLS cert validation gate for edge-proxy. also will add extra canary healthchecks for TLS handshake errors.
devon_choi: assigned follow-ups: investigate why cert rotation surfaced only in canary with v2.14.1, add unit/regression test.
maya_wong: customer impact: limited to canary subset in eu-west-1, estimated affected requests ~12k over 15m, no major accounts contacted support. notifying platform-incident channel and support.
pagerduty-bot: INC-48291 acknowledged by maya_wong.
ops_shift_lead: handing off to night oncall @samir_lee for post-incident monitoring and writeup. samir — please triage postmortem, timeline, and action items.
samir_lee: taking handoff. will own postmortem and runbook updates. adding timeline notes now.
incident-bot: NOTE: AUTO-RETIRE in 2h unless reopened.
maya_wong: thanks team — large thanks to @devon_choi for quick repro and to @kena_hart for patch plan.
kena_hart: :thumbsup: will draft the postmortem template and include rollback commands + detection queries.
maya_wong: closing PD after postmortem drafted.
